the interface between the lung opacity and the adjacent cardiac border (right or left heart margin).", "Determine if the border is preserved (visible aerated lung rim separates the opacity from the heart) or obscured (opacity merges with/blends into the heart contour).", "Apply the silhouette sign: A preserved border indicates the lesion is not in direct contact with the mediastinal pleura/pericardium (e.g., peripheral lung, posterior lower lobe), whereas an obscured border indicates direct anatomical contact (e.g., middle lobe, lingula, or anterior segment of the lower lobe)."]}, {"category": "comparison", "trigger": "When evaluating interval changes in the azygos fissure or lobe on chest imaging following pneumothorax and lung reexpansion.", "steps": ["Identify the azygos fissure (curvilinear line in the right upper lung) and the azygos vein (teardrop-shaped opacity at the medial base of the fissure) on both baseline and follow-up images.", "Compare the prominence and thickness of the fissure line between the two timepoints, specifically looking for increased visibility or thickening in the post-reexpansion image.", "Distinguish transient pleural separation/thickening (manifesting as a more prominent fissure) from other changes like lateral shift of the lobe, absence of the vein, or new adhesions, which would present with different morphological features."]}, {"category": "comparison", "trigger": "When evaluating serial chest X-rays to determine the progression or resolution of extra-alveolar air (pneumomediastinum and subcutaneous emphysema).", "steps": ["Inspect the initial image for vertical lucent streaks paralleling the mediastinal structures (especially the left heart border and aorta) and radiolucent striations within the soft tissues of the neck, axillae, or chest wall.", "Examine the follow-up image specifically at the mediastinal contours and soft tissue planes to verify if these lucencies have disappeared and normal anatomical interfaces have been restored.", "Distinguish complete resolution (absence of all abnormal lucencies in both compartments) from partial resolution (persistence of air in either the mediastinum or subcutaneous tissues) or worsening (increased extent of lucencies)."]}]
